equation_request.abstract: We present a novel scheme for universal quantum computation based on spinless interacting bosonic quantum walkers on a piecewise-constant graph, described by the two-dimensional BoseHubbard model. Arbitrary X and Z rotations are constructed, as well as an entangling two-qubit cphase gate and a swap gate. Quantum information is encoded in the positions of the walkers on the graph, as in previous quantum walk-based proposals for universal quantum computation, though in contrast to prior schemes this proposal requires a number of vertices only linear in the number of encoded qubits. It allows single-qubit measurements to be performed in a straightforward manner with localized operators, and can make use of existing quantum error correcting codes either directly within the universal gate set provided, or by extending the lattice to a third dimension. We present an intuitive example of a logical encoding to implement the seven-qubit Steane code. Finally, an implementation in terms of ultracold atoms in optical lattices is suggested.

specification.problem: Emulate the universal gate set of the Bose-Hubbard quantum-walk scheme (dual-rail walker position qubits; Rx, Rz, CP, SWAP, local Z-basis measurement) as an ordinary n-qubit circuit, with a Steane-code encoding example. Lattice dynamics are not simulated.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Gate-level emulation on n logical qubits, one qubit each, no ancillas for the universal gate set. Smallest instance: 2 qubits with Rx and Rz on each and one CP(phi), then Z-basis measurement. The Steane [[7,1,3]] encoder is a secondary extension (7 qubits, no syndrome ancillas). Outside scope: the actual Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian on a piecewise-constant graph, the 3D lattice extension, the optical-lattice implementation, the linear vertex-count proof, and error-correction beyond encoding.

symbols.meaning: rotation angle for Rx or Rz
walker on left or right site of a two-vertex pair

equations.label: Rz from on-site offset
equations.description: Energy offset between the two sites of a pair gives a Z rotation.
equations.abstract_quote: Arbitrary X and Z rotations are constructed
equations.justification: The abstract claims arbitrary Z rotations; the explicit form is the standard rotation with an idealized Hamiltonian.

equations.label: Rx from tunneling
equations.description: Tunneling between the two sites for a time t gives an X rotation.
equations.abstract_quote: Arbitrary X and Z rotations are constructed
equations.justification: Tunneling Hamiltonian -J X on the pair gives \theta=2Jt; the abstract claims arbitrary X rotations.

equations.label: Controlled phase from Hubbard interaction
equations.description: The on-site interaction phase appears only when both walkers occupy interacting sites, i.e. on |11>. The sign is convention, and phi is tunable.
equations.justification: A cphase gate is claimed; the mapping to U t follows from the sketch's assumption that the interaction acts only on |11>.
assumptions: Single-qubit phases are compensated by Rz

equations.label: SWAP
equations.description: Exchanging the encoded positions of two walkers. It can be built from three CX gates.
equations.justification: The abstract names a swap gate; its action is standard.

equations.label: Z-basis readout probability
equations.description: Measuring qubit i in the computational basis corresponds to locating walker i. For X-basis measurement, apply H before measuring.
equations.abstract_quote: single-qubit measurements to be performed in a straightforward manner with localized operators
equations.justification: Local position detection corresponds to a computational-basis measurement.

registers.name: q
registers.role: one qubit per logical qubit, encoding the walker position on a two-site pair; qubit i is the i-th logical qubit

registers.name: c
registers.role: classical bits, measure(i,i); in Qiskit counts keys bits[::-1][i] is qubit i

steps.description: Apply single-qubit Rx(theta) and Rz(theta) rotations on chosen qubits.
Apply CP(phi) between the chosen pair of qubits (qiskit cp), and SWAP where connectivity requires it.
Optionally apply H before measuring a qubit in the X basis, then measure the needed qubits, or read the statevector if the task asks for it.

specification.measurement: Computational basis on each needed qubit i via measure(i,i). Unitary or statevector tasks take no measurements.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Reverse each counts key (bits[::-1]) so index i is qubit i. For the Steane extension, decode by a syndrome lookup table.
assumptions: Smallest instance is 2 qubits, since the task gives no scope
Dual-rail encoding, with 2 vertices per qubit
Idealized exact Hamiltonian evolution with freely tunable angles
One walker per qubit, no loss; the circuit is a plain qubit circuit
Gate-level circuit rather than a lattice simulation
Steane encoding uses the standard CNOT circuit; syndrome ancillas would need to fit under the qubit cap
